review.summary: The plan needs about 2,667 leads, a marketing budget of £298,667 and £4.8m of pipeline to deliver 48 wins and £1.2m of marketing-sourced revenue, which is 60% of the £2m target. Hitting that goal depends on turning 192 opportunities into wins at a 25% rate, so the plan is only as strong as its sales conversion.
review.constraint: The weakest stage is opportunity to won at 25%. Lifting it to 30% would save £49,778, the largest saving of the four levers tested, ahead of lead to MQL (£42,667), MQL to SQL (£33,185) and SQL to opportunity (£22,974).
risks: The 25% win rate is an assumption, and if sales converts fewer opportunities, the 48 wins and £1.2m revenue will not be reached without more spend or more pipeline.
With a four-month sales cycle, spend made now will not produce won deals until later, so any early shortfall in pipeline will show up in revenue only after a delay.
actions: Ask sales to confirm or challenge the 25% win rate using its own recent deal history before the budget is approved.
Test the cheapest levers first, such as improving lead to MQL and MQL to SQL conversion, and track whether each change reduces the £112 blended cost per lead or the cost per win of £6,222.
Shift the review from annual totals to monthly targets of 4 wins, 16 opportunities and 222 leads, and reallocate budget between channels if any channel falls behind its lead count.
